free_tier.stated: Ryzen Mini at EUR 3.95 a month on the cart's monthly term (EUR 10.95 quarterly, EUR 20.95 semi-annually, EUR 39.95 annually; EUR 3.33 a month derived on the annual term): 1 AMD Ryzen 7950X core, 1 GB RAM, 15 GB pure NVMe, 4 TB bandwidth, 10 Gbps uplink, 1 dedicated IPv4 plus a /64 IPv6, daily backup, Amsterdam. The range continues Ryzen Elite EUR 5.95 (2 GB, 30 GB, 8 TB), Bronze EUR 6.95 (2 EPYC cores, 4 GB, 40 GB, 8 TB), Platinum EUR 12.95 (4 EPYC, 8 GB, 80 GB, 16 TB) and Diamond EUR 25.95 (8 EPYC, 16 GB, 160 GB, 32 TB). The tracker row it lists is Platinum at EUR 12.95. The cart marks all five plans out of stock, and the EPYC cart prints all four billing terms per plan. Renewal: not published on any page.

egress.terms: monthly allowance with a hard throttle past it rather than an overage charge: 'Your network speed is reduced to 1 Mbps until the next billing cycle. No surprise overage charges.', quoted from the vendor FAQ
egress.free_allowance: 4 TB/month on Ryzen Mini; 8 TB on Bronze and Ryzen Elite, 16 TB on Platinum, 32 TB on Diamond

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: control panel with one-click OS reinstall, start/stop/reboot, bandwidth monitoring, manual backups, rDNS configuration and a VNC console; no API was stated on the page read; 7 Linux distributions supported and no Windows
chaining: EUR 3.95 for 15 GB of NVMe, 4 TB and a 10 Gbps uplink in Amsterdam is the cheapest 10 Gbps entry of the eight providers compared here, and the throttle to 1 Mbps at the cap instead of an overage invoice makes it safe to leave unattended: the failure mode is slowness, not a bill. On 2026-11-07 the vendor cart marked all five plans, Ryzen Mini through Diamond, out of stock, so none was orderable that day at these prices.
